_comment: Melee weapon ladder spec (#631). The melee counterpart to ranged_ladders.json.
The unit is SUSTAINED damage (DPS), not one blow. A lighter blade that swings faster can
out-damage a heavier one, so ranking on the displayed damage number gets those backwards.
See docs/features/melee-damage-model.md for how DPS is derived and what its limits are.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-20 across 364 Armory melee weapons and 858 troops, the
median best-DPS per engine tier ran 66, 64, 66, 67, 69, 69, 81, 82, 82, 69 for tiers 1 to
10. That is a 1.04x climb. Vanilla climbs 2.23x over five tiers (30, 50, 58, 60, 67). Troop
tier had almost no bearing on melee output, and the capstone tier was armed below tier 7.
THE ANCHOR. TAOM's tier-5 median of 69 already matched vanilla's tier-5 median of 67, so
the midpoint was never the problem and is held fixed. The curve below fans out around it at
vanilla's own slope of roughly +9 DPS per tier. Changing `curve` changes the whole mod's
melee power distribution; changing `anchor_tier` moves what stays put while you do it.
KINGDOM OFFSETS are carried over from tools/rebalance_weapons.py CULTURAL_POINTS, which is
the existing per-culture craftsmanship table, so faction flavour survives the flattening
fix. They are a percentage of the tier target, not flat DPS, so they scale with the curve.
The band is what counts as on-curve. Too tight and every roster is a finding; too loose and
the ladder does not mean anything. 0.25 leaves 46% of troops already correct.
_kingdom_comment: Percentage shift applied to the tier target for a troop of this culture. Keys are engine
culture StringIds, which is what a troop's culture= attribute carries: TAOM remaps several
vanilla ids (vlandia is Rohan, empire and battania are Dunland, aserai is Harad, khuzait is
Rhun, sturgia is Dale). A culture absent from this table takes the plain tier target.
LEGACY PATH. `craft` below replaces `kingdom_offset`, and `class_band` replaces `band`, wherever
the weapon's crafting template is known (it has a class limit and a `craft_column`). This table,
`band` and `ceiling` serve only a caller that passes no template.
_ceiling_comment: No weapon may out-sustain this, in DPS, except the hero blades named in the exempt list.
140 is vanilla's own demonstrated maximum: the hardest-sustaining vanilla melee weapon
measured 138 DPS. Holding TAOM to it is what 'no weapon too OP' means numerically. 65
_class_limits_comment: The most one weapon of a class may do, keyed by crafting template: `swing` and `thrust` are
the displayed damage of ONE blow, `swing_dps` and `thrust_dps` the sustained damage of that
attack. A weapon must be inside all four. null means vanilla has no such attack in the class.
WHY. The curve above is one DPS curve for every class, and nothing limited one blow. On
2026-11-14 a placeholder one handed sword met its tier-10 target of 119 DPS with a 140 swing,
and shield spears reached 123 per thrust. Most troops have 100 health (Mike, 2026-11-14): a
one handed weapon must not kill one in a single blow.
THE NUMBERS are the vanilla maximum per class, rounded, measured 2026-11-14 with
melee_catalogue over SandBoxCore and SandBox (261 weapons): one handed sword 103 swing (one
outlier, then 95 and 86), 54 thrust, 83 and 47 DPS; one handed axe 83 and 70; mace 71 and 58;
two handed sword 140 and 132; two handed axe 139 and 103; polearm 184 swing and 138 DPS, 49
thrust and 43 DPS; pike 42 and 35. Vanilla has five two handed maces (85 and 59), too few to
copy, so that class sits between the one handed mace and the two handed axe. Thrust on the
polearm classes is 60 rather than 49 because a couched lance is outside this model.
OneHandedPolearm is not a crafting template but the class of a spear's one handed mode: the
mode a troop with a shield thrusts in (its two handed mode is requires_no_shield), so a
shield troop's spear is judged on it (melee_catalogue.Priced.with_shield, 2026-11-16).
Vanilla's 55 such modes thrust 42 at most (median 32) and 35.4 DPS at most (median 25.8):
rounded up to 45 and 37. Judged on the 45 DPS two handed thrust instead, every shield spear
in vanilla's range read as under-armed.
A hero blade is held to its hero limit (the class limit plus its maker group's bonus, see
`hero_bonus`) and is exempt from `ceiling`.
_craft_comment: PER-CLASS TIER TARGET (2026-11-14). Part 1 stopped a raise at the class limit, but the shared
curve above passes the one handed limits near tier 6, so tiers 6 to 10 would carry the same
sword. TAOM has ten troop tiers (vanilla has six) and each class must spread over all ten:
target(class, tier, culture) = class_top x class_tier_fraction[tier] x craft[culture][column]
`class_top` is the larger of the class's swing_dps and thrust_dps that the weapon can use (null
ignored), so a thrust-only spear of template TwoHandedPolearm tops at 45 and a swinging polearm
at 138. A polearm that can do both takes its top from the swing only when its swing DPS is at
least its thrust DPS (melee_ladder.dominant_flags); a spear in the hand tops at the thrust.
`class_tier_fraction` is the share of the top a tier may reach, 0.58 at tier 0, 0.81 at tier 5
and 1.0 at tier 10 (2026-11-14, replacing the shared curve's curve[tier] / curve[10]). The craft
factor ranks each culture's smithing in three columns; the best culture in a column is 1.00 and
sits on the class top at tier 10. `craft_column` maps a template to its column. A culture not
listed takes `craft_default`.
THE TIER LIMIT. The same factor, class_tier_fraction[tier] x craft, also scales every class limit
(blow and DPS) for a weapon an ordinary troop carries: melee_ladder.tier_limit. The class limits
above are the tier 10 numbers, so a tier 3 recruit cannot carry a blade that only an elite may
swing. A hero blade keeps its hero limit at every tier.
Keys are the engine culture ids a troop's culture= carries (see _kingdom_comment), with one
exception: `craft_troop_prefix` maps a troop id prefix to a row, so the Black Numenoreans
(mordor_num_) are rated by mordor_numenorean while the engine still reads them as mordor.
Callers go through melee_ladder.craft_key. Source: the craft table in
docs/reviews/melee-class-limits-plan-2026-11-14.md, Recommendation 3, Mike's direction of
2026-11-14 (smithing decides where a culture sits in the vanilla range); the rows for
mordor_numenorean, umbar, shaghana and feral_orcs and the vlandia polearm 1.00 were added on
2026-11-14 with the weapon and armour rebalance (#1271). No troop carries an Iron Hills
culture id, so there is no entry for one. A minor culture (southrhovanion, angaladh,
anduinvale, dorwinion, bluecraig) stays on `craft_default`.
`class_band` is the per-class window around the target. 0.15 is a first guess: the steps are
small for the low classes (a one handed sword gains about 6 DPS per tier at the top).
_under_tolerance_comment: A weapon under its carrier's band is accepted while it sits inside the band of a tier up to
`under_tolerance_tiers` below (melee_ladder.judge). The maintainer, 2026-11-16: a tier 6 troop is
better than a tier 5 one with the same weapon, because it swings faster and is better armoured.
Weapon skill adds blow damage (+0.15% per point one handed, 0.16% two handed, 0.07% polearm) and
attack speed (+0.07%, 0.06%, 0.06%): about 4 to 6% DPS per tier for swords and axes, 3% for
polearms, against weapon targets that rise 3 to 9% per tier. Over a band is never excused, and
restat_melee_blades.py still prices blades onto the exact target.
_exempt_comment: Named hero weapons, which are meant to sit above the curve. Keyed by BLADE PIECE, because
that is what a restat edits and what a shared blade drags along with it. Carried over from
tools/rebalance_weapons.py HERO_BLADE_IDS so the two agree on who is exempt.
_hero_comment: HERO LIMITS (2026-11-14). `hero_blades` lists the exempt blade pieces: exempt from the tier
target, never from a limit. A hero blade may sit above the plain class limit by its maker
group's bonus (DPS), and its blow limits rise in the same proportion. Mike: 5 to 10 DPS above
the vanilla maximum, never more than 10, the most for the best smiths.
`hero_makers` maps a blade piece to a group, `hero_bonus` a group to DPS. A hero blade with no
maker takes `other`. The grouping is the author's reading of the lore, for Mike to correct.
The five Noldor swords and the three Khamul blades were added on 2026-11-14: no troop carries
any of them and no other weapon shares their blade piece.
_exempt_troops_comment: Troops deliberately off the ladder, each with a stated reason. An entry naming a troop that
no longer exists, or one that is now on curve, is itself a finding: a stale allowlist reads

exempt_troops.cave_troll: A troll is a monster, not a soldier. Its weapons are scenery-scale and deliberately slow, and the creature's threat comes from its own attacks and its mass rather than from its kit sustaining tier-10 DPS.
exempt_troops.hill_troll: The same monster rule as the cave troll: the hill troll carries its own war hammer (wm_hill_troll_2h_hammer_a; head weight 0.875, set 2026-09-26 so the engine prices it at the cave mace's 86 Blunt and swing speed 28) on its own 3.6 m skeleton.
exempt_troops.mordor_uruk_shieldguard: A spear and shield troop whose name says so. The roster pass of 2026-11-16 found no other in-band shield-safe spear in Mordor's pool and picked an Uruk halberd that thrusts; rca-black-uruk-weapons-2026-11-07 F1 left a halberd as its main weapon as an open option, not a decision. Keep its Gundabad spear until that is decided.
